message.content:
### The “Best” Sushi Restaurants in Los Angeles (as of 2026)

Below is a curated list of the most highly regarded sushi spots in Los Angeles, based on Michelin stars, industry awards, food‑critic reviews, and local buzz.  “Best” can mean different things—authenticity, innovation, value, or atmosphere—so I’ve grouped the picks by what they’re known for.

| # | Restaurant | Neighborhood | What Makes It Stand Out | Michelin/Other Accolades |
|---|------------|--------------|------------------------|--------------------------|
| **1** | **Sushi Gen** | Little Tokyo | Legendary for its *tuna* and *sashimi* quality; the chef’s meticulous knife work is a must‑see. | 1 Michelin Star (2024) |
| **2** | **Sushi Park** | West Hollywood | Known for its *omakase* experience and a menu that balances classic and avant‑garde pieces. | 1 Michelin Star (2024) |
| **3** | **Sushi Tetsu** | West Hollywood | A hidden gem with a *chef‑driven* menu; the *tuna sashimi* is often cited as the best in town. | 1 Michelin Star (2024) |
| **4** | **Kazu** | West Hollywood | A modern take on Japanese cuisine; the *tuna sashimi* and *tuna nigiri* are crowd‑pleasers. | 1 Michelin Star (2024) |
| **5** | **Sushi Ota** | West Hollywood | A family‑run spot that offers a *traditional* sushi experience with a focus on *seasonal* fish. | 1 Michelin Star (2024) |
| **6** | **Sushi Kappo** | West Hollywood | Combines *kappo* style service with a *sushi bar*; the *tuna sashimi* is consistently praised. | 1 Michelin Star (2024) |
| **7** | **Sushi Saito** | West Hollywood | A newer addition that has quickly earned a Michelin star for its *precision* and *freshness*. | 1 Michelin Star (2024) |
| **8** | **Sushi Nori** | West Hollywood | Known for its *creative rolls* and *tuna sashimi* that balances flavor and texture. | 1 Michelin Star (2024) |
| **9** | **Sushi Tatsu** | West Hollywood | A *family‑owned* spot that offers a *tuna sashimi* that’s both affordable and high‑quality. | 1 Michelin Star (2024) |
| **10** | **Sushi Katsu** | West Hollywood | A *budget‑friendly* option that still delivers a *tuna sashimi* that rivals pricier spots. | 1 Michelin Star (2024) |

> **Why these spots?**  
> • **Michelin Stars**: All listed have earned at least one Michelin star in the 2024 guide, a strong indicator of quality.  
> • **Tuna Sashimi**: Every restaurant on the list is celebrated for its tuna sashimi—whether it’s the buttery texture of *maguro*, the delicate *toro*, or the robust *akami*.  
> • **Location**: Most are concentrated in West Hollywood and Little Tokyo, making them easy to reach from most parts of LA.

---

#### Quick Tips for Visiting

| Tip | Explanation |
|-----|-------------|
| **Reserve Early** | Especially for the Michelin‑starred spots, reservations can book up months in advance. |
| **Ask for Omakase** | If you’re looking for the chef’s best selection, request an omakase; it often includes the finest tuna sashimi. |
| **Check Seasonal Menus** | Tuna quality varies with the season; ask the chef about the freshest catch. |
| **Try the “Tuna Sashimi”** | Even if you order a roll, ask for a side of tuna sashimi to experience the pure flavor. |
| **Consider the Atmosphere** | Some places are ultra‑intimate (Sushi Gen), while others are more casual (Sushi Tatsu). Pick what fits your vibe. |

---

#### Bottom Line

If you’re after the **most acclaimed tuna sashimi** in Los Angeles, **Sushi Gen** and **Sushi Park** are the top two picks—both hold Michelin stars and are consistently rated as the best in the city.  For a more modern twist or a budget‑friendly option, **Sushi Kappo** and **Sushi Tatsu** are excellent alternatives.

Enjoy your sushi adventure! 🍣
